scenes.say: Eat carrots, and you'll never need glasses. Myth, or fact?

scenes.en: Carrots can't fix short sight, long sight or astigmatism.
scenes.say: It's a myth. Carrots cannot fix short sight, long sight or astigmatism. Those come from the shape of your eye.

scenes.en: Your body turns carrots' beta-carotene into vitamin A. The retina needs it to see in dim light.
scenes.say: But carrots do help. They contain beta carotene, which your body turns into vitamin A. Your retina needs vitamin A to see in dim light.

scenes.en: The carrot story spread in World War II, partly to hide that pilots used radar.
scenes.ta: இந்த கதை இரண்டாம் உலகப் போரில் பரவியது
scenes.say: Did you know? The carrot story spread during World War Two, partly to hide that British pilots were using radar.

scenes.en: Leafy greens like keerai, eggs, fish, colourful fruits and veg
scenes.say: For healthy eyes, eat a rainbow: leafy greens, eggs, fish, and colourful fruits and vegetables. Stay active, and don't smoke.

scenes.en: UV sunglasses outdoors. Keep sugar and BP in control.
scenes.say: Wear good sunglasses in strong sun, and keep sugar and blood pressure under control. If seeing at night suddenly gets hard, see an eye specialist.

scenes.en: Food can't replace them. Book an eye test.
scenes.ta: உணவு கண்ணாடிக்கு மாற்று அல்ல. கண் பரிசோதனை செய்யுங்கள்
scenes.say: If you need glasses, no food can replace them. Book an eye test today.
